Suggested Literature

  • Douglas B. West, "Introduction to Graph Theory". This book should cover all the main concepts discussed during lectures. If you check only one book, this should be the one.
  • Reinhard Diestel, "Graph Theory". Arguably more involved, it is often the book of reference.
  • Martin C. Golumbic, "Algorithmic Graph Theory and Perfect Graphs". Too dive deeper into the class of perfect and chordal graphs.

Grading Policy for Final Grade Calculation

Your final grade for this course will be primarily determined by your performance on the final exam. However, the midterm exam offers an opportunity to potentially boost your grade. The midterm is optional and will only be used to improve your final grade—it cannot lower it.Here’s how the final grade will be calculated:

  • Let Z be your midterm grade (0 if you don't take it).
  • Let Y be your exam grade.
  • Your final grade Z will be calculated as Z=max⁡{Y,0.3X+0.7Y}.

Office hours, questions, and exercises submissions

Exercises should be submitted as PDF files by 18:00 on Tuesdays, before Thursday’s lecture, directly to henri.ortmueller@unifr.ch.

If needed, contact us by email: henri.ortmueller@unifr.ch || clement.dallard@unifr.ch.
